answer.rationale: Write-path p99 rose shortly after the new build while settlement writes are also at the daily peak, so cause is not uniquely identified. Rollback is the leading action because the latency climb began after the release window and memory_b1 is the only playbook that restored a write/checkout path without dropping customer writes. Capacity (memory_b3) remains a live alternative if verification shows the archived rollback case was error-only or that peak headroom was the real stabilizer. Circuit breaking is rejected because failing open dependencies can lose writes, which violates the objective. Read-replica routing addresses reporting load, not the write path. No regional signal supports failover. Verifying b1 and b3 before commit; until those archives return, treat release-vs-load as unresolved.
